name: GS23612 - VPA-1 - Renewable energy generation through solar photovoltaic in Thailand
description:
The proposed VPA aims to increase renewable energy generation capacity via solar photovoltaic (PV) installation in public and private buildings. Thailand has immense potential for solar-based projects. While large-scale solar farms require large land-use, rooftop solar can utilize the space on the rooftops of buildings or in and around as captive ground-mounted solar installations within the premises of the buildings in cities. Thus, installing solar for buildings is a practical measure to reduce emissions and energy demand for cities.
The VPA entails the installation of rooftop and ground-mounted solar PV systems for captive (self-consumption) use in Thailand. The VPA will generate approximately 20,126 MWh annually and achieve 8,030 tCO2 in annual emission reductions.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals
poa_project_name: Low Carbon Cities and Carbon Market Development Project

name: Low Carbon Cities and Carbon Market Development Project
description:
The Program Development Objective is to (i) reduce carbon emission and cost of operation for Thailand, (ii) improve air quality, and (iii) tap into the potential of the carbon market to offset the cost of investments with short-term and no regret interventions that are proposed to be implemented in the coming years to enable immediate actions of stakeholders to move towards a green and climate-resilient future. The program aims to support Thailand to reduce carbon emissions and move towards a green and climate resilient future through the following interventions:
•	Increasing renewable energy (RE) generation capacity for captive consumption
•	Improving energy efficiency (EE) in buildings
•	Upgrading to LED streetlights 
•	Transition to electric vehicles
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals

name: Solar Electric Cooking Systems for Schools and Other Institutions in Tanzania
description:
The project provides solar electric cooking systems (SECSs) through subsidized and affordable long-term financing to schools and other institutions (e.g. hospitals) to completely replace firewood and charcoal for cooking with electricity from renewable energy sources.

The solar systems are designed to produce more electricity than is consumed for cooking over the year and are typically sized to meet the institution’s total annual electricity demand included the additional demand from electric cooking.

The SECSs include among others large efficient electric pots (e.g. up to 400 l) with heat insulation and automatic temperature control.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals

name: GS10789-GS10790-RVPA-92: Efficient and Clean Cooking for households in Zambia
description: This VPA deploys efficient improved cookstoves (ICS), reducing woody biomass consumption for Urban and peri-urban households in the Republic of Zambia. The scenario existing prior to the implementation of the project is the use of very inefficient traditional cookstoves or 3- stone fires, consuming a lot of non-renewable charcoal and firewood. The high biomass consumption has negative impacts on the environment leading to deforestation and land degradation, Greenhouse Gas Emissions (GHG) emissions, loss of soil fertility and soils’ reduced ability of water retention. Further, indoor air pollution through health-damaging pollutants while combusting firewood and charcoal result in diseases like e.g. pneumonia, stroke, ischemic heart diseases, chronic obstructive pulmonary diseases and lung cancer.

name: Proactiva CGA Iperó Landfill Gas to Energy Project
description: The project activity titled “Proactiva CGA Iperó Landfill Gas to Energy Project” encompasses the promotion of destruction and utilization landfill gas (LFG) (rich in methane) at the CGA Iperó landfill site. LFG destruction occurs in a high temperature enclosed flare and through its utilization as gaseous fuel for electricity generation (in engine-generator sets). Thus, besides methane destruction, the project activity also promotes generation of electricity by using renewable energy sources (with a total nameplate capacity of about 8.5 MW). The CGA Iperó landfill is located located in the border of Sorocaba and Iperó’s municipalities, in São Paulo State, Southeastern Region of Brazil.

description: The voluntary project activity (VPA) is a voluntary initiative by Unlocking Communities (UC) to distribute household water filters in Haiti. The target beneficiaries under the project will be the households which were earlier dependent on boiling using non-renewable biomass for safe drinking water. Unlocking Communities is a locally run organization working in northern and central Haiti. Distribution of household water filters which is a clean energy product as compared to the baseline, will reduce the GHG emissions by eliminating the need for water treatment through boiling. name: GS23562- VPA 1 The Future of Cooking in Zambia
description:
This VPA aims to support the energy transition and reduce charcoal consumption and related greenhouse gas emissions through the distribution of improved charcoal cookstoves and pellet gasifier cookstoves, applying a fuel-switch approach. By promoting the adoption of cleaner and more efficient cooking solutions, the VPA contributes to reducing reliance on traditional charcoal and lowering associated environmental and climate impacts.



The VPA will be implemented in Zambia, with a particular focus on the Copperbelt region, targeting urban and peri-urban areas. The activities are designed to generate positive impacts within local communities, with specific attention to supporting women’s empowerment through improved access to clean cooking technologies, reduced time spent on fuel collection, and enhanced livelihood opportunities.

In addition, the VPA includes the construction of water towers to ensure reliable access to safe drinking water, along with continuous capacity-building activities aimed at strengthening local skills, knowledge, and long-term socio-economic resilience.

poa_project_name: The Future of Cooking in Emerging Countries

name: The Future of Cooking in Emerging Countries
description:
The project aims to support the energy transition and reduce charcoal consumption and related greenhouse gas emissions through the distribution of improved charcoal cookstoves and pellet gasifier cookstoves within local communities. By promoting the adoption of cleaner and more efficient cooking technologies, the project contributes to lowering fuel demand, improving energy efficiency, and reducing environmental and climate impacts associated with traditional cooking practices.



In parallel, the project places strong emphasis on community empowerment by creating local employment opportunities, delivering technical and operational training, and investing in essential community infrastructure such as water towers and greenhouses. These activities are designed to strengthen local capacities, improve access to resources, and foster sustainable socio-economic development in the countries where the project is implemented.



The project contributes to the achievement of the following Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs): SDG 1 (No Poverty), SDG 2 (Zero Hunger) SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-Being), SDG 4 (Quality Education), SDG 5 (Gender Equality), SDG 6 (Clean Water and Sanitation), SDG 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy), SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth), SDG 13 (Climate Action), and SDG 15 (Life on Land).

name: Kuphatana - Acções Inclusivas para Florestas Sustentáveis ​​em Moçambique
description:
The Kuphatana project aims to reforest 1,000 hectares of highly degraded land in the Administrative Post of Murraça, Mozambique, to restore the local ecosystem and support the socio-economic development of nearby communities. The project adopts a participatory approach, integrating environmental restoration with diversified livelihood activities such as beekeeping and dried mango production to ensure long-term sustainability and community engagement.
Climate change mitigation/adaptation contributions
Carbon Sequestration: The project establishes a forest that serves as a carbon sink, sequestering an annual average of 8,925 tCO2e. Over the 40-year crediting period, the total estimated net benefit is 351,044.5 tCO2e.
Biodiversity Enhancement: By planting a mix of native species (Vachellia xanthophloea and Khaya anthotheca) alongside non-invasive Eucalyptus urophylla, the project restores habitats for local flora and fauna
Climate Adaptation through Livelihoods - Beekeeping: The project engages 15 families per year from adjacent villages, providing them with beehives and training. This creates a direct economic incentive for the community to protect the forest from threats such as uncontrolled fires or illegal deforestation, as the bee colonies rely on the trees for nectar.
Climate Adaptation through Livelihoods - Sustainable Value Chains: Establishing a local value chain for dried mangoes offers diversified, climate-resilient financial growth for local families.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals
